data.title: Green Card Woes Deepen for Indian Tech Workers
data.description:
Prachi Verma New Delhi: Thousands of Indian technology professionals pursuing US permanent residency face fresh uncertainty after the US suspended major technology companies, including Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCLTech, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe, from the permanent labour certification (PERM) programme, an important step in the employer-sponsored green card process.

The move could delay permanent residency plans for employees already facing years-long green card backlogs, immigration experts told ET. Those nearing the six-year H-1B visa limit without an alternative basis for extension could face more immediate challenges, they added. "The immediate impact is on employment-based permanent-residence sponsorship, not on the subsistence of existing H-1B status," said Rohit Jain, managing partner at Singhania & Co. Existing H-1B approvals, approved I-140 petitions and permanent-resident status are not automatically revoked by this measure, he noted.

Employees awaiting PERM, however, may "face indefinite green-card delays, retention uncertainty and possible six-year H-1B-limit complications," Jain said. Close to a million Indians, including dependents, are estimated to be waiting for employment-based green cards, most of them in the EB-2 and EB-3 categories, said Sukanya Raman, country head for India at immigration-focused law firm Davies & Associates. "These are people who have spent years on temporary status and followed every rule, and now their green card process is on hold because of a dispute they have no part in," she added.

The restrictions could also become a talent-retention challenge for IT companies. While the firms are free to employ existing H-1B workers, their ability to offer those employees a long-term immigration pathway is constrained, said Sahil Nyati, founder and CEO of Meritmap and Jinee Green Card. "Employees may increasingly evaluate employers based not just on compensation and career growth, but also on the stability of their immigration sponsorship," he said.

Companies are reviewing their existing immigration pipelines. "They are identifying employees most exposed to the restrictions and reassessing their workforce planning," Nyati said. PERM requires an employer to establish that no able, willing, qualified and available US workers exist, and that employment of the foreign worker will not adversely affect equivalent US wages or conditions.

According to experts, IT employers are likely to apply a three-pronged strategy to address this - hire more US citizens and permanent residents, expand offshore and nearshore delivery capabilities, and become more selective about international employees. "We may also see companies evaluate alternative immigration pathways, including O-1A visas for individuals with extraordinary ability and EB-1A or EB-2 NIW green card categories for employees who independently qualify," Nyati said.

data.title: RBI Raises Minimum Daily CRR Maintenance to 99%
data.description:
to drain surplus liquidity Our Bureau Mumbai|Kolkata: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has raised the minimum daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement for scheduled banks to 99% from 90%, effective from mid-October. The move is aimed at draining surplus liquidity in the banking system as the central bank shifts towards calibrated tightening amid a liquidity surplus of about 4 lakh crore.

In a notification on Friday, the RBI said banks will have to maintain a minimum daily balance of 99% of the CRR requirement from the fortnight beginning October 16. CRR is the amount of deposits banks maintain with the RBI without earning interest. The ratio currently stands at 3%, which means that out of every 100 of deposits, a bank has to keep 3 with the RBI without earning interest.

So far, banks have had the operational flexibility to maintain only 90% of the required amount without attracting penal action. "On a review of the current liquidity conditions, it has been decided to increase the minimum daily maintenance of the CRR from 90% of the requirement to 99% effective from the fortnight beginning October 16, 2026," the RBI said.

Bankers said the new measure will curtail operational freedom. "So far, in a fortnight, banks had the flexibility to maintain 90% of the required CRR amount for seven days and maintain 110% for the next half of the reporting fortnight so that the average comes out to 100%. That flexibility will now go as banks will mostly have to maintain 100% at all times.

Other than some operational changes, this new norm will not lead to any major changes for banks," said Gopal Tripathi, head-treasury and capital markets at Jana Small Finance Bank. The central bank has decided to raise the daily requirement instead of tinkering with the CRR rate, which, according to RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra's post-policy comments, is "the least preferred" tool. "RBI had offered CRR exemptions on FCNR (B) deposit inflows through the dedicated foreign currency mobilisation programme, and therefore any hike in the CRR would not drain the additional flows," said a treasury executive, who did not wish to be identified. In July 2013, the RBI had similarly increased the minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement to 99% from 70%, said people familiar with the matter.

data.title: D-St Breaks 8-Week Losing Run, Outlook Stays Cautious Though
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: Indian equities snapped an eight-week losing streak on Friday as easing crude oil prices helped stocks rebound from the previous session's sharp selloff. The BSE Sensex rose 879.09 points, or 1.23%, to close at 72,472.33, while the NSE Nifty 50 advanced 288.65 points, or 1.30%, to settle at 22,520.45. For the week, the Sensex gained 0.8%, and the Nifty rose 0.4%. "Global cues offered some relief as Brent crude eased from its recent highs," said Ajit Mishra, senior vice president-research, Religare Broking.

Brent crude oil prices fell to $102.90 per barrel on Friday, down roughly 1.32% from the previous day when prices went past $104 a barrel, due to supply concerns in the Middle East. However, elevated global bond yields and persistent foreign fund outflows continue to weigh on sentiment, keeping the outlook cautious.

The sharp sell-off in the previous session and uncertainty surrounding the global macroeconomic environment reinforce the need for a measured approach, Mishra said. Foreign portfolio investors were net sellers of equities worth 3,569 crore on Friday, while domestic institutional investors were net buyers to the tune of 4,743 crore.

The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield was trading at 5.27% on Friday, below the 5.34% level it hit last week, its highest since 2002. The yield, which has risen 120 basis points in 2026, could rise to 6%, the highest since 2000, on concerns over high oil prices and the growing US public debt, Dan Ivascyn, chief investment officer at bond fund manager Pimco, told the Financial Times.

At home, the Nifty Midcap 150 index advanced 1.37%, and the Nifty Smallcap 250 gained 0.49%. Both indices, however, ended the week marginally lower, declining 0.19% and 0.08%, respectively. "We expect volatility to remain elevated as markets navigate this phase of correction and consolidation," said Kamlesh Shroff, founder, The Omniscient Securities.

He advised investors against chasing short-term momentum, recommending a focus on stock fundamentals, earnings visibility and disciplined investment strategies. On the technical front, the 22,350-22,330 zone could act as immediate support for the Nifty, according to Sudeep Shah, head of technical and derivatives research at SBI Securities. "A decisive move below this zone could trigger renewed selling pressure towards 22,200. On the upside, the 22,660-22,680 zone, coinciding with the 10-day EMA, could act as an immediate hurdle."

data.title: GSFC Seeks Partner for Green Ammonia Factory in Gujarat
data.description:
Shambhavi Anand New Delhi: Gujarat State Fertilizers and Chemicals (GSFC) is looking for a joint venture partner to set up a green ammonia plant with an annual capacity of at least 500,000 tonnes at its Sikka facility in Jamnagar, Gujarat, as India steps up efforts to replace fossil fuel-based ammonia used in fertiliser manufacturing.

The Gujarat government-promoted company is looking at joining hands with Indian and overseas companies, investors and consortiums to develop the project, which it aims to commission before December 2030. GSFC is seeking partners who can bring investment, technology and renewable energy expertise, along with long-term purchase commitments from potential customers.

The company is particularly targeting export markets in Europe, Japan and South Korea. According to the company's proposal, the project would require about 2-3 gigawatts of solar and wind power capacity to produce an estimated 90,000-100,000 tonnes of green hydrogen annually, which would then be used to manufacture ammonia. GSFC plans to sell about 90% of the proposed output to overseas and domestic customers, while using the remaining 10% in its own fertiliser operations. The proposed joint venture structure allows GSFC to hold up to 51% equity, although the final terms will depend on discussions with prospective partners.

data.title: US Green Card Curbs may have Little Impact on Indian IT Cos
data.description:
Suspension from Permanent Labour Certification Tanya Pandey & Surabhi Agarwal New Delhi: The four Indian IT services companies suspended by the United States Labour Department from the employment-based green card process-Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech-together recorded just 61 certified Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) filings in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 (Oct 1, 2025-June 30, 2026), with HCL America recording 59 certified cases and TCS only two.

Infosys and Wipro had no recorded cases in the period and neither did US-headquartered Cognizant. In the previous fiscal year, the number for the top Indian IT companies was 1,429. An ET analysis of US Department of Labour data shows that while American technology companies are bigger users of the programme, which allows foreign workers on H-1B visas to apply for permanent residency or the green card, employers in non-tech sectors such as food, meat and seafood were among the programme's biggest users.

TCS CEO K Krithivasan told ET on Friday that the suspension would have no impact on the company's business model or delivery of client projects, noting that its applications to convert H-1B visa holders to green-card holders had been in the single digits annually over the past two years. "We have close to 40,000 people in the US, and more than 50% of them are permanent residents or citizens," he said, adding that TCS files such applications occasionally when clients want the company to retain an employee for the long term. Foreign workers can stay in the US on an H-1B visa for six years, after which they have to return or apply for a green card. Consider the data for fiscal 2025. Of the 15 largest filers that year, five were technology companies and 10 were non-tech employers.

data.title: Food Industry Warns of Supply Shock as Super El NiÃ±o Threatens Crops
data.description:
Jayashree Bhosale Pune: India's food industry is warning of a potential supply shock in 2027 as a developing Super El NiÃ±o threatens to disrupt crop production, squeeze supplies and fuel food inflation beyond this year's monsoon season. "We are not so much worried for the next few months.

What concerns us is the next year-2027," said Bimal Kothari, president of the Indian Pulses and Grains Association, as the rabi chana harvest emerges a key determinant of the price of pulses. Sugar producers fear two difficult seasons ahead. "We are afraid that 2026-27 and 2027-28 can be extremely challenging for sugar production and availability," said Dilip Patil of the Indian Federation of Grain Energy.

Scientists have also warned of rising temperatures, heat stress and higher water demand. Commodity and weather experts have warned that India needs to plan for the long-term impact of El NiÃ±o. "The structural inflation risk in sugar is a 2027 problem, not a Diwali 2026 problem and the window to prepare for it is the next six months," sugar experts Dilip Patil and Shekhar Gaikwad wrote in their note on the sector-A Comfortable Diwali, an Uncomfortable 2027-presented to the Reserve Bank of India recently. "The 2026-27 balance sheet carries very little buffer, and the real inflation test will arrive in mid-2027, not in October 2026." The duo predicted that the ex-mill sugar prices could cross 50 per kilogram during June-October 2027 as the thin closing stock becomes the market's focal point.

On October 5, the El NiÃ±o-induced sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean set a new record, and are predicted to increase further. Former earth sciences secretary Madhavan Rajeevan said the country needs to prepare well in advance. "We should expect continued influences of this strong El NiÃ±o during the coming months," he said on X. "The ensuing winter could be warmer than normal, followed by a potentially hot and challenging pre-monsoon season, with an increased risk of severe heat-wave events." As prices of tur, chana, urad and yellow peas have already risen, the industry is more worried about the next year. "The real challenge is 2027. We need to see how the rabi plantation takes place.

We have drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka, both the states are important for chana," said Kothari. There are concerns about production of oilseeds, in which India is already import dependent.

Expect a big impact on sugar and oilseeds output from the Super El NiÃ±o, said Atul Chaturvedi, director, Shree Renuka Sugars and head of the Asian Palm Oil Alliance. "Among oilseeds, soyabean and groundnut seem to be in serious trouble, while sugarcane in Karnataka and parts of Maharashtra is drying up due to water scarcity," he said. "Domestic edible oil and sugar production is bound to suffer significantly during kharif. It would be interesting to see how this drought is going to impact rabi and beyond." data.title: MD bats for data centre space , says demand and healthy returns could make it a strong long-term biz
data.description:
'CORRECTION OF PRICING architecture AN INDUSTRY PROBLEM' People have to pay for consumption... Entry-level, inclusive plans have to stay where they are Shashwat Sharma MD & CEO, Bharti Airtel Airtel ARPU Will Cross 300 Very Soon, Need to Upgrade Customers, says CEO Kiran Rathee New Delhi: Bharti Airtel expects its average revenue per user (ARPU) to cross 300, helped by a surge in the share of postpaid customers to 20% over the long term from about 8% now, chief executive officer and managing director Shashwat Sharma said. "I believe it's around the corner... We can go much beyond 300 as well," Sharma told ET in his first interview since taking charge early this year.

Airtel currently has an industry-leading ARPU of 264. The company had 30 million postpaid subscribers as of June 30, accounting for about 8% of its customer base, and added nearly 1.05 million postpaid users during the quarter, its highest quarterly addition. It is betting on initiatives such as Fastlane and tweaking of tariffs to nudge a segment of its about 346.5 million pre-paid subscribers to upgrade to postpaid. "We believe we need to upgrade a lot of customers," Sharma said, describing postpaid upgrades as "a great lever in the industry." Postpaid accounts for about 12% of Airtel's revenue, he noted.

The quarterly pace of postpaid additions has accelerated from roughly 800,000 to about 1-1.1 million in the reported first quarter, an increase of around 30%. When asked about Airtel's recent tariff hike of 50 for postpaid plans, Sharma said, "People have to pay for consumption... Entry-level, inclusive plans have to stay where they are." His comments point to two opportunities for revenue growth: persuading more subscribers to choose richer postpaid packages and restructuring industry tariffs so that customers pay more as their data consumption increases.

Airtel recently launched its Fast Lane service, promising superior network quality based on 5G-slicing technology. The carrier is also seeking to drive upgrades through packages combining data, family connections, entertainment and international roaming benefits. Sharma said family plans offer particular value when households add second and third connections.

The opportunity, he said, lies in offering differentiated experiences that encourage customers to upgrade. Citing Indonesia and the Philippines as examples, Sharma said tiers of plans ranging from small to extra-large and a better pricing structure could allow the industry to sustain annual ARPU growth of 5-7%.

Asked whether Reliance Jio's upcoming public market listing could lead to fewer discounts and a change in telecom pricing, he said, "I think that's a big capital market event in the country. It's an industry problem." Beyond mobile services, Sharma expressed confidence in the data centre business. Asked about the planned expansion to 1 GW of capacity, he said anchor demand and healthy returns could make it a strong long-term business. "The business has very healthy returns," he said, explaining that while capital is invested upfront, returns accrue over a long period. "It pays off for 20-25 years." Himanshi Lohchab contributed to this article

data.title: West Asia Conflict Takes Some Sheen Off Bengal Puja Pandals
data.description:
Writankar Mukherjee Kolkata: The West Asia crisis is casting a shadow over West Bengal's 65,000 crore Durga Puja economy, with major organisers reporting a 10-20% drop in corporate sponsorships this year as companies rein in festive marketing budgets to cope with rising input costs and heightened volatility.

Several large national brands, traditionally among the biggest sponsors of community pujas in Kolkata, have cut spending on below-the-line activities, including sponsorships, promotional kiosks and outdoor advertising, organisers and industry executives said. Kolkata-based brands are stepping up to fill the gap, but their increased spending is insufficient to offset the shortfall in funding from national corporations, puja organisers said.

Parle Products vice president Mayank Shah said the biscuit maker has cut its Puja branding budget by 10-15% this year due to cost pressures. "We want to ensure that selling prices or MRPs are not increased at a time when demand is shaping up well," said Shah. "However, there is a fresh round of input cost pressure, so we have to balance it through internal efficiencies, absorbing a bit and reducing our promotional budget." Angshu Mallick, executive deputy chairman at Fortune edible maker AWL Agri Business said brands are cutting costs as the outlook remains uncertain due to West Asia volatility. The company has been a major sponsor of Bengal's Durga Puja.

LG, Daikin, ITC, Emami, Dabur, PepsiCo, Reliance Consumer Products, Coca-Cola, Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo ranked among the prominent sponsors of Kolkata pujas.

This year, however, most have cut back on spending on below-the-line activities. Corporate funding is 10-15% lower than last year, said Saswata Basu, vice president of Forum for Durgotsab, an association of community pujas in Kolkata and its suburbs. "A lot of national sponsors are silent," said Basu. "Some want LED signages for outdoor advertising, but only a few pujas have managed to organise it." The Puja festivities officially begin this Saturday and will continue for ten days, with peak celebrations next week.

Kolkata has around 3,000 community pujas, while West Bengal has around 45,000. Local brands are seeking to capitalise on the festival. Lux Industries, Bisk Farm and Spencer's Retail have stepped up promotional efforts, with Bisk Farm increasing its Durga Puja marketing budget by 50% year-on-year.

data.title: Poonawalla Fincorp Q2 Net Up Five-fold
data.description:
SOARS TO 375 CR on strong loan growth Our Bureau Mumbai: Poonawalla Fincorp's second-quarter net profit rose more than five-fold to 375 crore from a year earlier, as rapid loan-book growth lifted interest and fee income and helped operating profit more than double.

The non-bank lender's profit after tax rose 405.2% year-on-year in the quarter ended September 30, from 74 crore a year earlier. Profit increased 21.8% quarter-on-quarter from 308 crore in the preceding quarter. Net interest income, including fees and other income, climbed 75.6% year-on-year to 1,589 crore.

Cross-sell income rose to 118 crore from 68 crore, while servicing income increased to 91 crore from 37 crore. Assets under management rose 55% year-on-year to 74,008 crore. New products, including prime personal loans, gold loans, education loans, consumer durable loans, commercial vehicle loans and shopkeeper loans, accounted for 28% of second-quarter disbursements.

These businesses disbursed more than 4,400 crore during the quarter. Speaking to analysts, MD and CEO Arvind Kapil said growth was being accompanied by margin expansion. He said yields on new disbursements expanded by about 20 basis points in the second quarter, following an increase of about 50 basis points in the preceding quarter.

Higher yields on earlier disbursements were also flowing through to the overall portfolio, he said. Kapil also highlighted the expansion of the commercial vehicle business to more than 1,250 channel partners, the strengthening of education-loan origination through an instant-sanction platform, and the scaling up of the consumer durable network to 20,000 dealers across 360 locations. The company's gross non-performing asset ratio improved to 1.2% from 1.6% a year earlier. The lender's capital adequacy ratio stood at 18.7%, while total borrowings were 58,865 crore. Its cost of borrowing increased to 7.7% from 7.7% a year earlier.

data.title: IT Cos Surge Despite US Immigration Curbs
data.description:
Our Bureau Mumbai: IT stocks surged on Friday, with the Nifty IT index gaining more than 3%, as investors brushed aside fresh uncertainty over the US government's move to bar eight technology companies, including five from India, from participating in a programme linked to employment-based green card applications.

OpenAI's lower-than-estimated revenue run rate and Tata Consultancy Services' (TCS) relatively firm September-quarter results also helped boost sentiment in the sector, which has been grappling with worries about AI-related business disruptions.

The Nifty IT index's Friday performance was its biggest single-day gain since August 28. TCS shares rose 4.2%. HCL Technologies and Infosys gained around 3% each, while Wipro rose about 2.7% and Tech Mahindra advanced around 1.5%. "The rally in Indian IT stocks appears to reflect factors beyond TCS' Q2 results, which offered some reassurance on earnings resilience but no clear demand inflection," said Kunal Bajaj, research analyst at Choice Institutional Equities. "We see the rally as reflecting earnings resilience and easing AI-disruption concerns more than a fundamental recovery." Media reports cited OpenAI telling investors that its annualised revenue run rate in September was nearly $50 billion, lagging the nearly $70 billion figure indicated in earlier reports. "OpenAI's lower-than-previously indicated revenue run rate, largely reflecting differences in calculation and comparability rather than a clear demand slowdown, may also be easing concerns around AI-led disruption to traditional IT services and highlighting opportunities in enterprise AI implementation, integration and modernisation," said Bajaj.

The IT index has slipped nearly 8% from its August highs, retreating from a 17% rally since early July. The extent of the surge in IT stocks on Friday came as a surprise, as market participants were expecting a sell-off in response to the US government's decision to suspend IT firms from availing the Permanent Labour Certification Programme (PERM), which allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency. "One of the major reasons this news did not hold much gravitas when Indian markets opened is because most Indian IT firms in the US, such as Wipro, TCS and Infosys, owing to stricter regulations and higher costs associated with H-1B visas, have hired fewer personnel from outside the US," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services. Bajaj said the PERM suspension will have a limited immediate impact as it affects the employment-based green card pipeline, not existing H-1B work authorisation. The IT index is down 24.6% so far in 2026, compared with a 13.8% decline in the Nifty. Analysts, however, are not rushing to conclude that the worst is over for Indian IT stocks.

data.title: Gold Prices Fall Nearly 4% in a Month, Spurs Selective Buying
data.description:
Sutanuka Ghosal Kolkata: Gold prices have fallen nearly 4% in a month to about 1.47 lakh per 10 grams from 1.53 lakh, prompting selective buying ahead of the peak festive and wedding season as consumers look to make the most of the decline while remaining cautious about overall purchase costs. Lightweight designs, studded pieces and old-gold exchanges are gaining traction, according to industry executives. "The recent correction has encouraged some buying interest in India, although consumers remain price conscious," said Darshan Desai, CEO of Aspect Bullion & Refinery.

He said volatility is expected to persist, with the US economic data, Federal Reserve commentary and currency movements influencing prices, even as festive buying provides some support to the domestic bullion market. Jewellery demand remains resilient across price segments. CaratLane managing director Saumen Bhaumik said that consumers are more deliberate with their spending but remain interested in both value-conscious and premium jewellery.

The extended festive and wedding calendar, along with sustained appetite for diamonds and everyday jewellery, is keeping market sentiment positive, according to him. Mangesh Chauhan, managing director, Sky Gold & Diamonds, which manufactures jewellery for leading brands such as Tanishq and Malabar Gold & Diamonds, said festive and wedding demand were expected to remain healthy, supported by strong business-to-business orders from wholesalers and continued store expansion by jewellery retailers. "While prices are elevated, their relative stability in recent months has given consumers greater confidence to plan their purchases," he said.

However, buyers are increasingly seeking affordability without compromising on design. There is a growing preference for lightweight, lower-carat and design-led jewellery, while old-gold exchanges are allowing consumers to acquire new designs within their budgets, said Chauhan. Studded jewellery is also gaining popularity among younger buyers, prompting manufacturers to expand their offerings in this category.

Supriya Kataria, founder of Kumari Fine Jewellery, said that rising prices were making consumers more selective rather than deterring them from purchasing jewellery altogether. Buyers are showing greater interest in lightweight pieces, lower-carat options and versatile designs that balance aesthetics with affordability. Consumers are also comparing gold prices, making charges, promotional offers and exchange values more closely, with brand trust playing an important role in purchase decisions, she said.

The shift is likely to be more pronounced in discretionary purchases, while weddings, festivals and family milestones continue to underpin demand. Old-gold exchanges are emerging as an important means of managing purchase costs, allowing households to use the value of existing jewellery toward new purchases. With the festive and wedding calendar extending over the coming weeks, industry executives expect demand to hold up, though purchase decisions may take longer as consumers balance emotional spending with budget constraints.

data.title: Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall in Florida — WSJ
data.description:
By Joseph Pisani

Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Fla., Friday night, bringing heavy rains, damaging winds and the possibility of life-threatening flooding to the region.

"Buckle down at this point," Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said. "Don't be getting out on the roads."

The Category 2 hurricane hit the U.S. Gulf Coast around 9:30 p.m. Eastern time with 105 mph winds, pulling out trees and knocking down power lines.

More than 500,000 customers in Alabama and Florida were without power Friday night, according to PowerOutage.com, which tracks outages. Utility companies said they would send out crews to make repairs when it was safe to do so.

"Residents in these areas should have a safe room to ride out the storm and prepare for long-duration power outages," the National Weather Service said.

Forecasters warned storm surges could reach as high as 5 feet in parts of Alabama and Florida, moving rising water inland from the coastline. Even normally dry areas near the coast could see dangerous surges.

As much as 8 inches of rainfall is expected this weekend in southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and southwest Georgia, increasing the risk of flash flooding, the weather service said.

The hurricane is expected to weaken as it moves inland Saturday, "but Isaias is expected to continue producing gusty winds well inland," the National Weather Service said.

Isaias is the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 in what has been a relatively quiet season.

data.title: Kuwait selects consultant for $7.1mln real estate re-tendering contract
data.description:
Kuwait Authority for Partnership Projects (KAPP) has selected a preferred bidder for a 2.15 million Kuwaiti dinar ($7.1 million) consultancy contract to prepare feasibility studies and oversee the re-tendering of 23 real estate projects on state-owned land, according to local Arabic-language newspaper Al-Qabas.

The preferred bidder was selected from three shortlisted international consulting consortia, the report published on Thursday said.

data.title: Politically motivated decisions will deeply harm US: Indian-American Congressman Thanedar on Trump's H-1B, Green Card move
data.description:
Michigan, Oct. 10 -- Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar has criticised the Trump administration's decision to suspend certain companies from the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) programme, opposing restrictions affecting H-1B visa holders seeking Green Cards and warning that the move could harm the United States' economic innovation.

In a post on X on Friday (local time), Thanedar, a member of the US House Homeland Security Committee, said he strongly disagreed with the administration's decision to suspend the ability of H-1B visa holders working for major technology companies to apply for Green Cards.

"As a proud immigrant and a member of the Homeland Security Committee, I strongly disagree with the Trump Administration's decision to suspend the ability for H-1B visa holders who work for major tech companies to apply for Green Cards," Thanedar said.

He said H-1B workers were highly skilled professionals who made significant contributions to the American economy, adding that the programme played a key role in maintaining the country's global leadership in economic innovation.

"H-1B workers are highly skilled workers who make incredible contributions to America, and this program is a key way our country continues to be the world's leader in economic innovation," he said.

Thanedar called on the Trump administration to use existing laws to address fraud and abuse, increase the Green Card cap and expand funding for training American workers in the technology sector.

"If the President truly wants to combat fraud and increase economic innovation, he should use existing laws to curb fraud and abuse, increase the Green Card cap, and increase funding to train American workers in the tech sector," he said.

He further warned that decisions driven by political considerations could undermine the country's technological competitiveness and its ability to counter China's growing influence.

"Making politically motivated decisions about these important programs that help tech companies maintain America's world-class innovation and to effectively stand up to increasing Chinese aggression will deeply harm America," Thanedar added.

His remarks come amid a broader debate in the United States over the H-1B visa programme and the Trump administration's action against companies applying for permanent labour certifications for foreign workers.

On Thursday (local time), US Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the suspension of certain major technology and IT outsourcing companies from the PERM programme, citing multiple active federal investigations. The companies named included Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini, along with US technology companies Microsoft and Adobe.

Sonderling said the department would neither accept new applications nor process pending permanent labour certification applications involving the companies.

The announcement followed remarks by US Vice President JD Vance, who alleged widespread fraud in the H-1B visa programme and argued that companies should prioritise American workers. Vance specifically cited Microsoft, alleging that the company had laid off American employees while benefiting from thousands of H-1B visas and Green Cards.

Meanwhile, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified on Friday that the suspension of certain companies from the PERM programme was distinct from the H-1B visa programme and did not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents.

During a weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the decision could, however, affect the permanent-residency process of eligible employees at the companies concerned.

"The suspension of PERM application does not by itself affect the validity of H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents," Jaiswal said, adding that "there could be some impact on the permanent residency or green card process of eligible employees of the affected companies."

Responding to Vance's remarks about the programme, Jaiswal said comments that failed to recognise the contribution of Indian professionals to the American economy were unwarranted.

He also criticised the terminology used to refer to foreign workers, saying, "Resorting to terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations is deeply offensive."

The MEA emphasised that the movement of skilled professionals benefits both countries by supporting innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation.

"Talent mobility adds value to both economies, that is, the economies of India and the United States. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness, and job creation," Jaiswal said.

"The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries," he added, reiterating India's position that talent mobility remains an area of mutual benefit for New Delhi and Washington.

data.title: RBI revises forex derivative rules: What changes for transactions, cancelled contracts
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on October 10 announced regulatory measures for the foreign exchange market, including restrictions on rebooking cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts, a reduction in transaction thresholds and the introduction of a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR).

The measures were announced through two circulars, A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 25 and A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 26, with the stated objective of ensuring the orderly functioning of the foreign exchange market.

Restrictions on rebooking cancelled contracts

Authorised dealers will not be permitted to allow users to rebook any foreign exchange derivative contract involving the Indian rupee, whether deliverable or non-deliverable, if it has been cancelled with any authorised dealer after the issuance of the directions.

Rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity will continue to be permitted, subject to existing regulatory provisions.

Threshold reduced to $5 million

The RBI has reduced the threshold for undertaking foreign exchange derivative transactions to hedge contracted exposures without establishing the existence of the underlying exposure from $100 million to $5 million equivalent across all authorised dealers.

The corresponding threshold for taking positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee, without establishing the existence of underlying exposure, has also been reduced from $100 million to $5 million equivalent across all recognised stock exchanges taken together.

Additional documentation requirement

Authorised dealers will be required to obtain and retain an undertaking from users entering into rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts to hedge contracted exposures. The undertaking must confirm that the same underlying exposure has not been hedged with any other authorised dealer.

Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve introduced

The RBI has introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve requirement for rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts with a notional value exceeding $2 million equivalent.

Authorised dealers will be required to maintain a cash reserve with the RBI equal to 20% of the rupee equivalent of the notional amount of each such transaction.

The reserve requirement will apply to rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts undertaken to hedge current account exposures where the user purchases foreign currency against the rupee.

The RBI said the measures are intended to strengthen market discipline, ensure appropriate risk management and maintain an orderly and transparent foreign exchange market.

data.title: Trump Announces Deal With Putin, Says Russia Will Supply Diesel To US — 'Lower Prices For Americans... Is My Greatest Priority'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump said Russia will initially supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the U.S. and global marketplace, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and a million tons immediately thereafter.
  • He said the potential supply could grow substantially further depending on the condition of Russia’s diesel refineries.
  • According to Trump, Russia could ultimately deliver an additional three million tons of diesel fuel “within a short period of time.”

President Donald Trump said Saturday that he reached a “highly successful” agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin that could bring a major new supply of diesel fuel to global markets as the administration looks to push energy prices lower.

Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the arrangement would involve multiple waves of Russian diesel shipments, while touting what he described as a broader effort to bring down fuel costs for Americans.

“Between our total control of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, diesel prices for Americans and, indeed, the world, will be coming down, in record numbers, and fast!” he said.

Russia To Send Millions Of Tons Of Diesel, Says Trump

Trump said Russia will initially supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the U.S. and global marketplace, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and a million tons immediately thereafter.

Trump said the potential supply could grow substantially further depending on the condition of Russia’s diesel refineries.

According to the president, Russia could ultimately deliver an additional three million tons of diesel fuel “within a short period of time.”

That would bring the total volume Trump outlined to as much as 4.8 million tons, although the timing and actual delivery of the later shipments remain dependent on refinery conditions.

“Lower prices for Americans, especially our great farmers, ranchers, and truckers, is my greatest priority. This is a very big and important announcement,” Trump added.

Trump Links Diesel Prices To Strait Of Hormuz

Trump also tied the announcement to the broader energy situation surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, saying the U.S. has “TOTAL CONTROL” of the strategic waterway.

The president argued that the combination of control over the Strait of Hormuz and additional Russian diesel supplies could put significant downward pressure on fuel prices.

The comments come as energy markets remain highly sensitive to disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most important routes for global oil and fuel shipments.

Trump also added a separate warning on Iran, declaring: “Additionally, it must be understood, that Iran will not have a Nuclear Weapon!”

Crude Oil Prices Rise

Crude oil prices rose last week, with the U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures expiring in November rising 0.6% to $91.66 a barrel after a 1.41% fall the week before. Brent crude futures expiring in December rose 2.42% this week, hovering around $104.42 a barrel after a 3.47% increase the week before.

The United States Oil Fund ETF (USO) declined about 0.4% on Friday, while the ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil ETF (UCO) fell about 0.4%.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, was flat; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged up by 0.01%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) rose 0.02%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Jewellers pitch lure of natural diamonds amid lab-grown challenge
data.description:
Bengaluru/Mumbai, Oct. 10 -- Indian jewellers are stepping up their luxury pitch for natural diamonds this festive and wedding season, playing up their rarity and lasting value as cheaper lab-grown stones vie for the same consumer cohort. With natural diamond prices under pressure, jewellers are looking to attract more buyers and create new occasions for purchases in a market that's still largely untapped.

India is the world's second-largest market for natural diamond jewellery after the US, accounting for 12% of global demand, according to De Beers, global diamond mining and jewellery giant.

The diamond market is seeing mounting pressure. De Beers' average realized rough-diamond price fell 32% to $105 a carat in the first half of 2026, while smaller, lower-quality natural stones remained under pressure from lab-grown diamonds. The miner has also paused production at its Venetia mine in South Africa for two years to cut costs, even as India remains a robust market.

In India, De Beers is trying to expand the occasions for buying natural diamonds, while widening their availability beyond large jewellery chains.

"We took a step back and said, okay, if I want to grow this market, almost create a surround sound, how would I do it?", Shweta Harit, global senior vice president of De Beers Group and chief executive Forevermark, told Mint.

De Beers is expanding diamond purchases beyond proposals and weddings, targeting occasions such as second piercings, friendship and new life stages. Its 'Love From Hubby' campaign features an empty-nester couple, while 'Love From Dad' positioned a second piercing as a new occasion for natural diamonds. "Otherwise, you're really going to be stuck at some point in proposals or maybe weddings," Harit said.

For the festive and wedding season, De Beers is positioning natural diamonds around legacy and preciousness, including a campaign with Jaipur's Maharaja Sawai Padmanabh Singh and a Forevermark campaign featuring Princess Diya Kumari. "We really believe that natural stones have aura and power," Harit said.

The push extends to retail. Forevermark had 10 stores in India by July and plans to reach 20 by the end of 2026 and 100 by 2030. De Beers has also created the Indian Natural Diamond Retailers Association, or INDRA, with the Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council to bring smaller jewellers into the category.

Harit said about 60% of India's jewellery market remains unorganized, with many smaller retailers having generations of experience selling gold but less familiarity with diamonds.

The low penetration leaves room for further growth, Harit said. She estimates around 12% of jewellery pieces in India contain diamonds, compared with about 70% in the US. "Typically, you start with penetration, so you start with that. Then you get into frequency, so you want to buy more often. And then, you price up," she said.

Titan partnered with designer Rahul Mishra to showcase Tanishq's latest natural diamond collection, first presented at this year's Paris Couture Week, with the collection focused on highlighting the rarity and beauty of natural diamonds.

"We were always clear that natural diamonds will have its appeal, especially in a country like India, where preciousness plays a big role," said Ajoy Chawla, managing director of Titan Co. Ltd. "People do expect their jewellery to have a certain value retention. Overall, the store of value is important."

Tanishq has rolled out diamond experience centres in about 200 stores, where customers can study natural diamonds and understand their difference from lab-grown alternatives. The company is also shifting the conversation towards sparkle and visual appeal.

Titan's studded jewellery business is showing that the strategy is translating into demand. In its June quarter earnings call on 7 August, Chawla said the product mix was "swinging upwards towards more studded scale" and called it an important driver for the jewellery division. Titan's studded jewellery grew in the mid-30s in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 (Q1FY27), and the company said buyer growth in studded jewellery continued to outpace gold jewellery.

The momentum continued into the September quarter, with Titan reporting early-30s growth in studded jewellery in its Q2 update on 6 October, even as the overall jewellery portfolio grew 21%.

At the same time, Titan is not betting exclusively on natural diamonds. It launched beYon, its lab-grown diamond brand, in December 2025. Senco Gold and Diamonds has Sennes, while Trent has Pome under Westside, giving some of India's largest organised jewellery and retail groups a presence in both natural and lab-grown diamonds.

Lab-grown diamonds cost roughly one-tenth of a natural diamond of the same size/carat. They, however, do not have any resale value, and jewellers typically do not accept them for resale.

"You get a sense that you're not caught up in the semantics of the 4Cs," Chawla said, echoing similar marketing efforts by Indriya. "4Cs is such a dry way to describe a diamond. What matters is-what is the brilliance, the light performance, how do you see it come alive in front of you?"

To be sure, the 4Cs refer to the cut, colour, clarity and carat weight, making the global standard for evaluating diamond quality.

The bottom line, Chawla said, is that natural diamonds are one-of-a-kind, unlike each other, and not a commodity. He compared them with Indian heritage goods such as luxurious hand-woven textiles, which are valued for the slight imperfections that handmade work by master craftsmen inevitably leaves behind. In June, Indriya ran a 'Sparkle Like No Other' campaign with brand ambassador Aditi Rao Hydari to promote natural diamonds.

The challenge for the industry is that lab-grown diamonds are rapidly gaining ground. The International Gemological Institute's consolidated certification revenue from lab-grown diamond jewellery rose 44% year-on-year in April-June, while natural-diamond jewellery certification revenue grew 2%. Lab-grown loose-stone certification revenue rose 25%, compared with 6% for natural loose stones, according to IGI's investor presentation.

IGI said the lab-grown jewellery segment has seen over 1,000 retail showrooms across India as new players enter the market, while large manufacturers are adding capacity.

Indriya is taking a similar approach, moving beyond the traditional 4Cs in its natural-diamond marketing campaign launched in June this year.

"The context is that the Indian jewellery market is worth Rs.800k crores, and in that large market, about less than 10% is currently diamond jewellery. It is a very small segment of the total market at this time," said Sandeep Kohli, chief executive of Indriya.

"As jewellery progresses more towards a combo of beauty and adornment along with investment and store of value, people will want more jewellery in their drawers. If only less than 10% of Indian customers have diamond jewellery, they will want variety," Kohli said.

"There is a big market for diamond-based jewellery in India, and there will be growth. There will be people who prefer something more precious, like natural diamonds. And there will be some who may want to go for lab-grown diamonds given their budgets," he said. "If the diamond business overall is small, the LGDs business is tiny. You have to see where the market settles."

Indriya is also rolling out diamond-studded versions of most of its designs. Its upcoming Padmika collection, for instance, will be available in both gold and diamond versions.

"Besides polki (uncut diamonds), diamonds have not been part of traditional jewellery. But look at a category like mangalsutra, the share of diamond-based jewellery in that category is higher than the average diamond share of jewellery overall," said Kohli.

The shift is filtering down to smaller jewellers. "The price correction is making customers more comfortable exploring diamond jewellery across a wider range of occasions and price points," said Supriya Kataria, founder of Kumari Fine Jewellery, based in Mumbai. Demand is strongest for lightweight, design-led pieces, with some customers trading savings for larger or better-quality stones, she said.

At Zen Diamond India, also headquartered in Mumbai, lower prices are bringing in more first-time buyers and encouraging existing customers to upgrade, said managing director Neil Sonawala. He expects natural diamonds to remain the key sales driver this season.

data.title: MAG 7 Voices: How Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta Reshaped AI This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is pushing to bring Nvidia’s AI computing platform to personal computers and has committed $1 billion over five years to U.S. scientific research.
  • Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella sees secure desktop environments as essential for AI agents, predicting that local and cloud-based intelligence will increasingly work together.
  • Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has emphasized Google’s integrated AI stack, while its new Gemini agent’s use of rival models highlights a more flexible approach.

The Magnificent Seven are no longer making the same bet on artificial intelligence. Microsoft (MSFT) wants them running securely on personal computers. Alphabet’s (GOOG, GOOGL) Google is building a cloud-based agent that can handle complex tasks and retain context. Meta (META) is putting its assistant into new devices, including a wearable pendant.

But the race to make AI more capable is running alongside a harder question for investors: how quickly can the technology generate durable revenue?

A Financial Times report on Thursday stated that OpenAI told prospective investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion, below the roughly $68 billion figure widely reported two months earlier.

The report attributed the gap in part to different accounting methods. Anthropic includes revenue from cloud partners such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, while OpenAI does not.

The distinction does not necessarily indicate a sudden deterioration in demand, but it has given investors another reason to scrutinize the numbers behind the AI investment cycle. Nvidia (NVDA) underperformed the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) so far this week, while Apple (AAPL) outperformed.

Washington is also trying to shape the next phase of the industry. President Donald Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as AI czar on Sunday to lead a “Super Intelligence Force,” which has 120 days to report.

Nvidia: Bringing The AI Stack To The Desktop

Clayton’s 120-day reporting clock is also running. For investors, the bigger question is whether the next round of AI launches can show a credible path from impressive capabilities and heavy infrastructure spending to durable revenue. OpenAI’s latest revenue disclosure has brought that question back to the center of the AI trade.

The pitch extends Nvidia’s business beyond the data centers that have driven its growth. RTX Spark laptop preorders opened Wednesday ahead of an October 16 release, and Nvidia previewed a Windows version of its GB300-based DGX Station with 748GB of memory.

Huang also tied Nvidia’s strategy to the administration’s science agenda. At a Washington event Thursday, the company committed $1 billion over five years to U.S. scientific research, quantum computing, healthcare and energy security under Trump’s Genesis Mission.

“With a $1 billion investment, NVIDIA is putting advanced Super Intelligence in the hands of America’s scientists,” Huang said, describing the effort as a way to turn “scientific leadership into industrial leadership.” The language echoes the administration’s “Super Intelligence” branding, while Nvidia continues to sell the computing systems needed to support those ambitions.

Microsoft: The Sandbox Is The Product

Microsoft made its Execution Containers generally available Wednesday, giving AI agents a restricted environment in which to operate without unrestricted access to a user’s data or ability to take actions on a device. Anthropic, OpenAI and Nvidia will use the technology.

“We needed to make the desktop the most secure place for agents to execute,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said. He added that “hybrid intelligence will be everywhere,” suggesting that local computing and cloud services will increasingly work together rather than compete as mutually exclusive options.

Hardware is only part of the story. Microsoft has guided for Windows OEM and Devices revenue to decline in the high teens in fiscal 2027, while demand for its Azure cloud service continues to exceed available supply. Moor Insights analyst Anshel Sag said the memory crunch could make local AI a purchase mainly for customers with the budget to afford it.

Alphabet: One Agent, Multiple Models

Google Cloud introduced its Gemini agent Thursday, presenting it as a single assistant for work that takes “objectives, not instructions.” The system can coordinate sub-agents on tasks that may run for hours or days. It remains in private preview, with broader availability across Workspace expected later.

A notable feature is its ability to select the model best suited to a task. The agent currently uses both Google’s Gemini and Anthropic’s Claude models.

Wall Street is watching the hardware behind that strategy. Wells Fargo raised its price target on Alphabet to $417 from $411 and projected external sales of its tensor processing units (TPUs) at $9.2 billion in the third quarter (Q3) and $11.5 billion in the fourth quarter (Q4). Those estimates include hardware installed in customers’ own data centers.

Meta: Free AI, Unanswered Questions

Meta is taking a different approach by distributing its AI assistant through consumer devices. Muse is free for now while Meta explores its options, and IDC analyst Meredith Whalen said “the real question is trust.”

Microsoft may help Meta expand the assistant’s reach. Microsoft’s announcement said Muse will integrate with its execution containers and receive a native Windows app, although no release date, pricing or user target was provided.

Amazon: Making The Case For $220 Billion In Spending

Amazon’s (AMZN) AI spending drew attention through comments from AWS CEO Matt Garman on the a16z podcast Thursday. Garman said AWS’s largest customer accounts for only a single-digit share of revenue and put Amazon’s 2026 capital expenditure near $220 billion. He also noted that startups contribute 30% to 40% of AWS revenue, with Trainium capacity sold out for the next year.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos offered a more personal view of AI’s potential in an interview with Fox News. He said AI could allow some people to decide, “I can support my family working three days a week,” and promoted Prometheus, the startup he co-leads.

Apple: Cook Steps Back, Ternus Faces The AI Test

Apple’s week was defined by the transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus. In an interview with The Independent, Cook said he stepped down on September 1 partly to give Ternus “some wind at his back.” He also called the iPhone Duo amazing, while Ternus remained largely out of the spotlight.

Apple has confirmed a second fall event for Octo ber. 13. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman expects the company to introduce a smart-home hub with a screen, a new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV, all built around Siri AI.

Tesla: Terafab Takes A New Turn

Tesla’s (TSLA) AI plans also shifted during the week. CEO Elon Musk confirmed Saturday that talks with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) about the Terafab chip complex were “just discussions, but something may come of it.” By Wednesday, Musk said Tesla and his other companies would build and operate Terafab themselves, with TSMC potentially limited to subleasing space.

Musk also accused unnamed “oligarchs” in India of blocking Starlink’s launch to protect a “monopolistic chokehold” on connectivity, according to comments reported Wednesday.

Tesla’s robotaxi operations continued to expand. Service hours in Austin moved to 11 p.m., with Musk explaining the limit as “literally trying to avoid grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark.” Round-the-clock service is tied to the planned release of FSD v15 this month.

Texas records reportedly show Cybercab registrations at 319, up from 169, although Austin remains the only public robotaxi market. Tesla also faces an October 30 deadline to provide the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration with sworn answers about Cybercab safety certification.

The operating numbers offered a brighter spot. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, beating the 461,974 consensus estimate by 5.3%. Energy-storage deployments totaled 13.7 gigawatt-hours, below the 15.9 GWh estimate. Tesla reports earnings on October 21.

What To Watch

Slated for next week is Apple’s event on Tuesday. Tesla’s Roadster demonstration is scheduled for Thursday, followed by the October 16 start of RTX Spark laptop shipments and Surface Laptop Ultra deliveries.

Clayton’s 120-day reporting clock is also running. For investors, the bigger question is whether the next round of AI launches can show a credible path from impressive capabilities and heavy infrastructure spending to durable revenue.

data.title: RBI announces special dollar window for three PSU oil companies from October 12
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs), effective October 12, 2026.

The facility will cover Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), the central bank said in a press release dated October 10.

Under the arrangement, the RBI will sell US dollars to the three companies through designated banks. The facility will remain in place until further notice.

The central bank said the decision was taken after assessing current market conditions.

The move comes as the rupee remains under pressure, having traded at record-low levels in recent sessions.

On Friday, October 9, the domestic currency appreciated 17 paise to close at 96.71 against the US dollar, recovering from Thursday's (October 8's) close of 96.88.

Forex traders attributed Friday's recovery to a softer US dollar, easing crude oil prices and likely intervention by the central bank.

Oil marketing companies require dollars to pay for crude oil imports. The special window will provide a dedicated channel for meeting the entire daily dollar requirements of the three public sector companies, according to the RBI's announcement.

The central bank did not specify the pricing mechanism for the dollar sales or the volume of foreign exchange expected to be supplied under the facility.

data.title: Zetwerk eyes Rs.27,000 crore IPO valuation as over 30 investors weigh anchor book
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Zetwerk, a business-to-business (B2B) manufacturing platform, is preparing to tap the public markets as it seeks to capitalise on growing investor interest in India's industrial growth story.

The company is looking to launch its initial public offering (IPO) in the next few weeks at a valuation of around Rs.27,000 crore ($3.1 billion), according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The IPO is expected to comprise a fresh issue of Rs.2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs.2,200 crore by existing investors.

Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), Norway's central bank, and the asset management arms of Goldman Sachs, SBI and HDFC are among more than 30 foreign and domestic investors considering participation in Zetwerk's anchor book ahead of its IPO, said the first of the two persons cited earlier, both speaking on condition of anonymity.

"There is a diversified book that includes mutual funds and key FIIs. The company is likely to be valued at around Rs.27,000 crore," said the second person, adding that more investors would be added to the anchor book by Sunday night.

The company said it would announce the price band of the IPO on Monday, 12 October.

Other marquee investors that have expressed interest in the anchor book include SBI Pension Fund, BlackRock, Edelweiss Asset Management and Norges Bank, Norway's central bank.

The company is expected to file its red herring prospectus (RHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) within the next two weeks. the people said.

Norges Bank and SBI Pension Fund said they had no comments, while Abu Dhabi Investment Authority declined to comment. Zetwerk did not immediately respond to Mint's email seeking comment. Mint also reached out to SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC AMC, Edelweiss AMC, Goldman Sachs AMC, and BlackRock for comment but did not receive a responses by press time.

Founded in 2018 by Amrit Acharya, Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Vishal Chaudhary, Ankit Fatehpuria and Rahul Sharma, Zetwerk runs on its proprietary software platform, Zetwerk OS, which manages sourcing, production planning, supplier coordination and project execution. The company operates through its own facilities and a network of third-party manufacturers, supplying products to a wide range of sectors, including utilities, renewable energy, consumer electronics, artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, space and defence, oil and gas, industrial automation and aerospace, both in India and overseas.

Zetwerk recorded an estimated operating revenue of Rs.15,900 crore in fiscal year 2026 (FY26), up 24% from fiscal year 2025 (FY25), Inc42 reported in June, citing a rating rationale from Crisil Ratings.

Zetwerk is preparing to enter the public markets at a time when investor sentiment remains subdued, particularly towards technology stocks. The Nifty IT index has fallen 24% so far in 2026, significantly underperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined 14%. The weak market sentiment could make investor demand and pricing key determinants of the success of Zetwerk's IPO, market participants said.

In an October report, Axis Direct said that "the IT Services is likely to report relatively moderate earnings growth (in Q2FY27), as global demand remains cautious."

However, ramp-ups in large deals, outcome-based engagements and rising AI-led spending should lend some support. Margins are expected to remain mixed, with wage hikes, AI investments, deal ramp-up costs and acquisitions weighing on profitability, partly offset by rupee depreciation and productivity gains, the brokerage added.

Since its founding, Zetwerk has raised a total of $931 million across 20 funding rounds as of 27 September, according to Tracxn data, with the last round raised early this year valuing it at $4 billion. Zetwerk is backed by investors including Greenoaks Capital, Khosla Ventures, Accel, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Peak XV Partners, Avenir Growth Capital, and Baillie Gifford.

The Bengaluru-based company has appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital, JM Financial, Avendus Capital, Pantomath Capital, and the Indian arms of HSBC, Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs as merchant bankers for its IPO.

Recent technology listings have seen mixed fortunes. ArMee Infotech, which listed on 30 September, opened flat but ended its debut session 21% lower. Fractal Analytics listed at a nearly 3% discount to its issue price on 16 February and closed the day down about 6%. In contrast, ESDS Software Solution made a strong debut on 4 September, listing at a premium of more than 76% and ending its first trading day up 109%.

Zetwerk's clients span a range of industries, from industrial heavyweights such as L&T, NTPC and Indian Oil to consumer electronics brand boAt and global companies such as Siemens, Acer and Schneider Electric. Other clients include National Aluminium Company Ltd (Nalco), CG Power Solutions, Nordex, Bharat Bijlee and Mortenson.

data.title: Stronger BoP outlook to keep Rupee far more stable; FY27 surplus seen at USD 97-100 billion: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- India's external position exhibits significant resilience as a robust balance of payments (BoP) projection provides substantial support to the domestic currency, according to a research report by ICICI Bank. The report projected that the country's BoP surplus will expand sharply to reach between USD 97 billion and USD 100 billion in the financial year 2026-27 (FY27).

The research findings attribute this positive trajectory to steady capital receipts, manageable trade parameters, and expanding external reserves, which together create a protective cushion against global macroeconomic volatility and spillover risks.

In its macroeconomic evaluation, the ICICI Bank research report said: "A bigger change is the far more stable performance of the domestic currency compared with the sharper depreciation episodes seen earlier in the year."

On the current account front, higher remittances up 24 per cent year-on-year in the April-July period and steady services export growth of 8.5 per cent year-on-year in the April-August period cushion the goods deficit.

With average crude oil prices near USD 94 per barrel, the merchandise goods deficit is projected at USD 387 billion to USD 400 billion, keeping the current account deficit between 1.2 per cent and 1.6 per cent of gross domestic product.

"Overall, we see BoP surplus of USD 97-100bn in FY27 now compared with a large deficit seen in last two years," the report said.

Macroeconomic growth remains firm, expanding by 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of FY27, supported by exports, investments, and manufacturing activity. Overall annual economic growth is estimated at 7.1 per cent. Headline inflation faces upward pressure from lower monsoon rainfall and sowing deficits, bringing expected inflation to 5.0 per cent and prompting potential policy tightening.

"In the near-term, the stronger dollar profile and higher oil prices could continue to keep the INR under pressures, but RBI's active dollar selling should ensure a much stable trading environment for the domestic currency," the report noted.

"Given the large FX inflows and stronger FX reserves (USD 780bn), the central bank is in a much better position to curb the excessive depreciation pressures unlike earlier periods," the report added.

The central bank holds a forward dollar book of USD 137 billion as of July-end. On a 40-currency real effective exchange rate basis, the Indian currency remains undervalued, with USD/INR projected to trade within a range of 94 to 96 in the near term.

data.title: Isaias weakens to Category 1 hurricane after Florida landfall, NHC says
data.description:
Hurricane Isaias rapidly lost windspeed on Friday, weakening into a Category 1 event after making landfall near Destin, Florida, the US National Hurricane Center said, but warned of danger from storm surges and floods as power links snapped.

The hurricane was about 65 miles (105 km) west-northwest of Panama City, Florida, packing maximum sustained winds of 90 mph (150 kph), the NHC said in its most recent advisory.

The agency warned against a life-threatening storm surge affecting the Gulf Coast as dangerous hurricane conditions and flash floods spread inland.

The hurricane is expected to cross Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley on the weekend, the agency added.

Nearly 380,000 people in Florida and more than 210,000 in Alabama were left without power as the storm hit shore, the website Poweroutage.us showed.

"Emergency declarations have been approved in Florida and Alabama to ensure federal resources are available to respond to Isaias," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on X.

Florida's emergency services urged residents to shelter in place and watch for hurricane conditions across the state's north after Isaias hit land as a category 2 storm.

data.title: Trump Sets Nov. 5 Hearing For Lisa Cook Over Alleged Mortgage Fraud As Her Lawyers Question Legitimacy of Probe
data.description:
Earlier this week, Donald Trump established a "committee of inquiry" to investigate whether Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook made false statements on mortgage documents, setting a Nov. 5 hearing on the allegations.

The panel includes the assistant to the president for economic policy, the chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and the director of the Office of Government Ethics.

Lisa Cook Can Present Evidence at Hearing

Trump’s memo says Cook should appear and can present arguments, written evidence and witness statements.

"As President, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law," Trump wrote in the memo.

On Friday, Cook’s attorneys, Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen, said in a statement that they have "grave doubts" that the hearing is legitimate, citing Trump’s repeated statements that he has already decided to fire her.

They said an objective review would find no mortgage fraud.

Supreme Court Ruling and Mortgage Fraud Allegations Explained

The dispute began in August 2025, when the Trump administration first sought to remove Cook.

Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte alleged that she had falsely listed properties in Georgia and Michigan as primary residences to secure lower mortgage rates.

In June, the Supreme Court ruled 5-4 to allow her to remain in office, finding that she had not been afforded sufficient due process to challenge the allegations.

After the ruling, Trump said in a June Truth Social post that the court sent the case back "on a strictly procedural basis" and that he would "take appropriate action immediately."

Cook denies the claims, saying she mistakenly called one of two properties a "vacation home." She has said the firing stemmed from Trump’s frustration over the pace of rate cuts.

data.title: Indian Navy to Commission Indigenous ASW Shallow Water Craft
data.description:
Build by Cochin Shipyard in Kochi, the Anti-Submarine Warfare Vessel Commissions at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai

Mangrol, the third Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) built by Cochin Shipyard (CSL), Kochi, is set to be commissioned into the Indian Navy on 12 Oct 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The ceremony will be presided over by Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command. The event will be attended by senior naval and defence officials, representatives from the Ministry of Defence and Cochin Shipyard, veterans and representatives of indigenous weapons and sensor manufacturers.

Named after Mangrol, a coastal town and prominent fishing harbour in Gujarat's Junagadh district, the ship carries forward the legacy of the erstwhile INS Mangrol (M85), a minesweeper that served the Indian Navy until 07 Apr 2004. The naming of the ship continues the Navy's tradition of preserving the legacy of its former warships.

Built with over 80% indigenous content, Mangrol reflects India's growing capabilities in warship design, construction and integration of advanced weapons and sensors. Constructed by CSL under the Government of India’s Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiatives, the ship marks another important step towards self-reliance in defence shipbuilding.

Designed to detect and counter underwater threats in coastal and shallow waters, Mangrol is equipped with modern weapons and sensors, including the Abhay Hull-Mounted Sonar, lightweight torpedoes, an indigenous anti-submarine rocket launcher and the Maareech Advanced Torpedo Decoy System. Powered by three diesel engines with waterjet propulsion, the ship offers high manoeuvrability for operations in shallow waters. It is also capable of undertaking underwater surveillance, Low-Intensity Maritime Operations and mine warfare-related tasks.

Mangrol will strengthen the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in coastal waters where larger warships face operational limitations. The ship can operate alongside maritime patrol aircraft, helicopters and other warships to detect and counter submarine threats. Its induction will enhance the Navy's ability to protect ports, harbours and coastal approaches while supporting wider fleet operations.

Amid growing underwater threats in the evolving maritime security environment, the commissioning of Mangrol marks an important milestone in strengthening the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in coastal waters.
